summary: Rabbi Soffer concludes the discussion on the midah of zehirut, focusing on the dangers of being a leitz and the importance of choosing the right company. He then introduces the next midah, zerizut, explaining that it is the active counterpart to being careful and requires overcoming our natural human tendency toward laziness.
questions: How does being a scoffer affect one's ability to do the right thing?
Why does Hashem sometimes send suffering to those who are not on the right path?
What should a person do if their friends make fun of them for trying to be careful?
How does our physical nature contribute to laziness?
Why is being lazy considered similar to being actively destructive?
